rename.residue: the residual difference is the correlation token (`int64_t` vs `rmw_request_id_t`), which is the divergence this row now carries. The RMW-ABI layer's own prose still says `send_reply` in `packages/core/nros-rmw-abi/docs/mainpage.md`, `rmw_entity.h`, `rmw_vtable.h` and the `docs/design/0035` slot table -- pre-existing phase-376 W3.b drift (the vtable SLOT has been `send_response` since then), left alone here because touching `rmw_entity.h` forces a bindgen regeneration of `packages/rmw/cffi/src/generated.rs`.

why:
LANDED 2026-08-27 (phase-379 W5). THE RENAME IS DONE and this row is retained for its history. What it recorded: rcl, rclcpp and rclrs all say `send_response`, our C already said it, and our C++ and Rust said `send_reply` -- with C contradicting ITSELF, `nros_service_send_response` sitting beside `nros_service_send_reply_raw`. Three languages, two words, one of them using both, and nothing about an RTOS preferring either. `send_reply`, `send_reply_raw` and `ServiceTrait::send_reply` all moved to `send_response`; the two C spellings and `Service::send_reply` survive as deprecated forwarders (their own rows), and the Rust trait method did not, because a required trait method is implemented by every backend and a defaulted forwarder there would turn a compile error into a runtime surprise.

WHAT STILL DIFFERS, and it is not the name: the correlation token. Ours is `send_response(int64_t seq_id, const ResponseType& resp)`; rclcpp's is `send_response(rmw_request_id_t& req_id, ServiceT::Response& response)`. Two arguments each, which is why the correlator now reports this arity-only rather than as a rename. `rmw_request_id_t` is a 16-byte writer GUID plus a sequence number, so a reply can be correlated across a client restart; ours is the bare sequence number, because the entity table is STATIC and a request cannot outlive its client, and because a DDS writer GUID does not generalise to the zenoh query id or the XRCE request id our other backends correlate with. Cheaper, and it cannot express a reply to a client that has been recreated. Same constraint, written up once, at `rust:RequestId`; see also `cpp:Client::create_request_header`.

AMENDED 2026-09-21 (phase-456 W5): ours moved to `nros::PollService<S>::send_response` with the storage it writes through. The correlation-token divergence recorded above is unchanged. See `cpp:Service::take_request` for why the split put the verb on the poll half and the upstream name on the dispatch one.
